column1: Waste Books|1800|0|10||7,6,7,4,8,9,5,8,5,9|Georg Christoph Lichtenberg|Aphorisms about observation, language and intellectual independence offer reusable distinctions rather than a sustained model. The source values their unfinished character; this supports learning density but limits causal depth and cumulative structure. First notebook publication began in 1800, not the 2000 reissue. Evidence: https://eprints.bbk.ac.uk/id/eprint/47626/1/Part%20One_MBrooker_PhDThesis.pdf

The Little Book of Talent|2012|0|0||6,4,7,5,8,7,3,6,8,7|Daniel Coyle|Condenses practice research into short suggestions for improving performance. The reader report supports high practical density, but the tips supply less evidence and boundary testing than a research synthesis. General learning advice is not a specialist technical curriculum.

How to Talk to Anyone|1999|0|0||5,3,6,3,5,7,1,5,7,5|Leil Lowndes|Offers concrete interpersonal habits and conversational cues. The source reports usable examples alongside ornate prose. These are heuristics for social interaction, with limited causal validation or systems content; poor fit is reflected in the score rather than exclusion.

You, Inc - The Art of Selling Yourself|2007|0|0||5,4,6,4,6,7,2,6,8,7|Harry Beckwith and Christine Clifford Beckwith|Short reflections connect considerate conduct with reputation and commercial trust. The reader report supports transferable communication lessons, but not a controlled account of which habits cause success. Personal positioning dominates over production or technical organization.

You Can Just Do Things|2026|0|0||5,5,7,4,6,6,3,6,8,7|Cate Hall and Sasha Chapin|Personal episodes motivate initiative, experimentation and challenging assumed constraints. These offer useful prompts but selection effects and omitted failures limit causal inference. Source report and publisher description inspected; a recent agency label alone does not establish V4. Original publication confirmed by the author: https://usefulfictions.substack.com/p/you-can-just-do-things-is-out-today

Voters as Mad Scientists|2023|0|10||6,6,6,6,7,7,4,8,8,7|Bryan Caplan|Essays apply incentives and asymmetric decision costs to political belief. The source supports clear arguments and varied examples, not comprehensive counterevidence. Political irrationality is central, so T12 applies. No inspected evidence establishes partisan recruitment as the dominant purpose.

Labor Econ Versus the World|2022|0|0||7,7,7,7,7,8,5,8,8,7|Bryan Caplan|Labor-market essays connect incentives, regulation and employment decisions. Analytical distinctions have cross-institutional use, although an essay selection is less cumulative than a sustained comparative study. The source describes reasoning rather than specialist calculation exercises. Author bibliography: https://bcaplan.com/

How Evil Are Politicians?|2022|0|10||6,6,6,5,7,7,4,8,8,7|Bryan Caplan|Short essays examine political incentives and moral judgments about governance. The source praises the reasoning, but does not demonstrate balanced treatment across the collection. Politics is the central topic; a provocative title is not evidence of V5 or V6.

Unboxing Bengaluru|2022|10|0|2022|6,7,6,6,7,6,7,7,8,7|Malini Goyal and Prashanth Prakash|Reported cases connect migration, software firms, venture capital and urban constraints. They offer industrial-cluster insights despite a celebratory city portrait and limited causal comparisons. T11 covers urban history. The foundation records first publication in November 2022; later publisher editions do not reset it. Evidence: https://www.unboxingblr.com/our-story ; https://www.penguin.co.in/book/unboxing-bengaluru/

No B.S. Time Management for Entrepreneurs|2004|0|0||5,3,6,3,5,7,2,6,7,5|Dan S. Kennedy|Opportunity cost, interruption control and prioritization provide a small reusable payload. The source explicitly reports a repeated message, so density is restrained. This is general personal-productivity advice rather than specialist technical training.

Introducing Pragmatism|2021|0|10||8,5,6,5,7,9,3,8,6,8|Cornelis de Waal|Explains differences within the pragmatist tradition and connects beliefs to inquiry and practical consequences. The source reports useful distinctions but demanding prose. A historical-conceptual survey qualifies without requiring formal proof training; philosophy is the dominant domain.

Pragmatism an Introduction|2012|0|10||8,5,6,5,7,9,3,8,7,8|Michael Bacon|Compares classical and contemporary pragmatists, including disputes about truth and social practice. Its distinctions offer intellectual transfer rather than technical procedures. Contents and specialist review support substantive coverage, but not paragraph-level density. Evidence: https://pure.royalholloway.ac.uk/en/publications/pragmatism-an-introduction/ ; https://ndpr.nd.edu/reviews/pragmatism-an-introduction/

The Developing World|2010|0|0|2010|5,7,6,5,6,6,6,6,8,6|Fredrik Härén|Cases of innovation across developing economies broaden the reader's comparison set. The source calls the account one-sided; selection of successful firms limits general causal claims. Historical endpoint is the contemporary development picture around publication, not an assumed timeless growth model.

Talent Is Overrated|2008|0|0||6,5,7,6,6,7,4,7,8,7|Geoff Colvin|Deliberate practice supplies a useful model of feedback and performance improvement. The source identifies a long introductory question-setting section and a more substantive middle. Claims about talent require separating training effects from selection and inherited differences; no blanket rejection is inferred from that limitation.

The Investor’s Manifesto|2009|0|10||8,6,8,7,8,8,5,8,8,8|William J. Bernstein|Explains diversification, costs and uncertainty in investing through a general argument for passive portfolios. The source supports clear numerical reasoning and substantial practical content. Finance is central; the purpose is an investor-facing explanation rather than a specialist mathematical curriculum.

Overachievement|2004|10|0||5,3,5,4,5,6,1,6,7,6|John Eliot|Performance coaching emphasizes trained automatic action under pressure. Sports examples and anecdotes offer limited transfer to decision contexts where deliberate analysis remains necessary. The reader report supports a recognizable heuristic, not validated general superiority of the proposed mindset.

The How of Happiness|2007|0|0||6,4,5,5,5,6,1,8,7,6|Sonja Lyubomirsky|Summarizes research-informed approaches to well-being. The source reports more conclusions than displayed experiments, limiting assessable evidence and useful learning per page. Its practical psychological payload passes V3, while domain fit remains weak.

The Culture Code|2006|0|0||4,5,5,3,5,6,2,5,7,5|Clotaire Rapaille|Cultural contrasts offer marketing hypotheses but risk turning selected associations into fixed national explanations. The reader report supports memorable distinctions, not representative sampling or robust causal tests. This weak evidence lowers E and M; inspected material is insufficient to establish a serious central factual failure for V1.

The Four Pillars of Investing|2002|0|10||8,7,8,7,7,9,5,8,8,8|William J. Bernstein|Connects market history, investor psychology, investment theory and commercial incentives. These layers explain diversification and cost control with durable strategic use. General explanatory synthesis qualifies; it is not primarily professional technical certification or a formal portfolio-theory course.

The Culting of Brands|2004|0|0||5,6,6,5,6,7,3,6,7,6|Douglas Atkin|Compares group belonging and brand allegiance to explain customer communities. This supplies organizational mechanisms, but analogy between cults and brands may hide important differences. The source describes marketing application; examining cult dynamics is not itself religious advocacy.

China in Ten Words|2010|10|0|2010|7,6,5,5,7,8,3,8,8,8|Yu Hua|Autobiographical essays connect language with social change, imitation and informal incentives in China. The source distinguishes revealing cultural observations from personal episodes. This is nonfiction despite the author's novels. Single-nation focus incurs T11; first Chinese publication predates the English edition.

Existentialism: A Beginner’s Guide|2008|0|10||7,4,5,4,6,8,2,8,6,7|Thomas Wartenberg|A conceptual survey supplies distinctions and context for existentialist arguments. The source found useful ideas but difficult presentation. General philosophical explanation is eligible without specialist formal training; the topic receives T12 and weak direct-domain fit.

Rule Makers, Rule Breakers|2018|0|0||7,7,7,6,7,8,4,9,8,7|Michele Gelfand|Compares tight and loose social norms across cultures, linking threats, coordination and tolerance. Comparative evidence and an explicit mechanism offer transfer, while broad national explanations need boundary conditions. The reader report challenges some answers but does not establish V1. Publisher confirms 2018, correcting misleading cached metadata: https://www.simonandschuster.com/books/Rule-Makers-Rule-Breakers/Michele-Gelfand/9781501152931

Connecting the Dots|2016|0|0||5,5,5,4,5,6,3,5,7,6|Sam Brinson|Synthesizes familiar learning ideas for a general audience. The source reports little new material for a reader who knows the underlying books; this limits marginal utility but does not by itself prove padding. Direct text coverage is insufficient for a high-confidence density judgment.

True Style|2015|0|0||7,4,4,4,6,8,1,8,8,8|G. Bruce Boyer|Essays explain traditions and judgments in men's dress. The source supports a measured historical-cultural treatment rather than specialist tailoring instruction. The transferable payload is modest but present in material, convention and contextual judgment; low domain fit is not an exclusion.
